sourceInformation.genre: Arcade multi-sport score attack: skateboarding, surfing, BMX
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer (WebGPU, WebGL2 fallback); Rapier 0.19.3; Web Audio API; Gamepad API; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub session client 1.4.0; HTML/CSS/JavaScript
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural flat-shaded coastal dioramas with ink outlines, sun-faded cream, coral, teal, and gold
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and NumberKeyframeTrack rider cycles, plus procedural wheels, spray and scenery motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-synthesized surf/chiptune music, effects, and Animalese-style gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1 parallel score competition for 1–4; standalone PeerJS/WebRTC rooms for 1–4; local 1–4 hotseat
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with software WebGPU; scripted complete festival, scoring, physics, gamepad stub, touch, pause, tuning, audio OfflineAudioContext, attract loop; official Hub harness at 2 and 4 players with latency/loss and host-leave; real two-page PeerJS; WebGL2 screenshots for visual inspection. Physical controller, real touch hardware and audible listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No source research and no web searches. Supplied AI Hub integration contract and runtime dependencies downloaded.

testingFeedback: Testing and review caught 20 implementation issues; all were resolved. Final validation passed 105 gameplay/input/audio/network checks and 10 packaging checks with zero failures. The issue log records each resolved issue.
5 could break startup, BMX recovery, or attract playback.
The scripted three-sport festival and official Hub harness, including four players and host departure, checked the whole scoring and session lifecycle.
The first software WebGPU screenshot was blank; state assertions and a separate WebGL2 visual pass were more useful.
engineFeedback: Three.js scene graphs and native AnimationMixer clips made procedural athletes, boards, bikes, scenery, and animation straightforward.
Yes. Early manual bundling caused a duplicate identifier, and software WebGPU screenshots were blank. Scoped bundles and WebGL2 visual checks resolved these.

promptFeedback: The controller-first philosophy, explicit sharing format, attract-mode requirement, and code-only audio encouraged a cohesive arcade game.
The no-internet research rule alongside mandatory linked multiplayer documentation required treating integration documentation as implementation input.
Making three different sports, all input modes, online rounds, procedural art/audio, and a single-file package feel consistent.
Clarify the documentation exception to the research restriction and give a target demo length.

aiHub.name: Californium Games
aiHub.description: Chase golden wave pockets, launch half-pipe tricks, and link BMX ramp combos in a sun-faded coastal arcade festival. Compete solo, pass the controller, or share an online room.
aiHub.controls: Stick / WASD / arrows to steer and pump; Cross / A / Space to pop; Square / X / J to grab; Circle / B / K to flip; Options / Esc to pause; touch drag and tap.
